newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow court turns down SIDANKO suit vs Rosneft.
newsitem.headline: Moscow court turns down SIDANKO suit vs Rosneft.

text.p: The Moscow Arbitration Court turned down the latest attempt by oil company SIDANKO to wrest back control of prize oil producer AO Purneftegaz from state oil holding company Rosneft, Rosneft and SIDANKO said on Monday.
The case was the third fought by SIDANKO for ownership of the producer, now officially called AO Rosneft-Purneftegaz.
Sibirskaya Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) was suing the State Property Committee -- Russia's privatisation ministry -- and state oil concern Rosneft.
But the ruling is unlikely to be the end of the bitter wrangle.
SIDANKO press spokeswoman Olga Sergeyeva said that the company intended to go to the appeal bench of the Moscow court, as soon it established the reason for the court turning down the latest action.
Rosneft legal department director, Valery Arefyev, said that the court's official decision on the reasons for turning down the suit would be ready by Thursday.
A 1994 government resolution awarded Purneftegaz to SIDANKO, but a later ruling shifted ownership back to Rosneft.
SIDANKO's main production units include Chernogorneft, Varyoganneftegaz and Kondpetroleum.
SIDANKO produced 20.81 million tonnes of oil in 1996.
Purneftegaz produced about eight million tonnes of oil in 1995, the last year for which figures were available.
